stem: When counselling parents about long-segment or whole aganglionic bowel, which major long-term problem should be discussed?

options.text: A normal long-term bowel course with no major sequelae

explanation: Intestinal failure is the major long-term problem to discuss in extensive aganglionosis. Long-segment or whole aganglionic bowel can lead to short bowel, prolonged parenteral nutrition, and related complications.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Additional Congenital Surgical Problems

optionExplanations.A: Correct because long-segment or whole aganglionic bowel can cause intestinal failure and other serious long-term complications.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because extensive aganglionosis does not reliably recover spontaneously and often requires surgery and ongoing care.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Hirschsprung disease is a disorder of the distal bowel, not the stomach alone.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because calretinin is used in diagnosis, not as a marker of later clinical resolution.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because extensive disease can have major long-term sequelae, including intestinal failure.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
